top3.headline: A wave of breaches and critical flaws hit the infrastructure agents run on.
top3.whyItMatters: Every agent key is a credit card with no fraud checks. One key per agent, spend caps and rotation are this week's to-do.

top3.headline: Agent Skills becomes an open standard, already in 70+ platforms.
top3.whyItMatters: Your team's know-how, written once as skills, now works across ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and Claude.

top3.headline: Four labs have shipped always-on agents in about 10 weeks.
top3.whyItMatters: Agents with their own computer are the new default. The decision is whom you trust with your accounts.

items.title: Anthropic hands Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation, the same home as MCP
items.takeaway: Anthropic is donating the Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation. Since December 2025, 70+ agent platforms have integrated it, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and VS Code.
items.soWhat: Skills you write for one agent now travel across vendors. Invest in a skills library, not in one tool.

image.alt: Screenshot of the X post: @ClaudeDevs on X

items.title: Black October: Railway breach leaked customer API keys as Node.js, PHP2Shell and GitLab flaws hit
items.takeaway: Railway disclosed a breach that may have exposed customer API keys and secrets. Critical Node.js, PHP2Shell and GitLab patches landed the same day. Vercel shipped firewall mitigations before the Node.js patch.
items.soWhat: Agent keys work like credit cards with no fraud checks. One key per agent, IP allowlists, rotate now.

related.name: X News: critical vulnerabilities on Oct 21

image.alt: Screenshot of the X post: @gregisenberg on X

items.title: ChatGPT Ads reach 89 countries, including 14 in Latin America
items.takeaway: OpenAI added 26 countries to ChatGPT Ads, among them Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Peru. More than 100,000 advertisers have used the platform in about eight months.
items.soWhat: Being found inside AI answers is now a paid channel. Marketing budgets need a line for it.

items.title: Claude Duet makes it four labs shipping always-on agents in about 10 weeks
items.takeaway: Anthropic launched Claude Duet, a proactive agent with its own VM and browser. It is US-only for now, with a Pro/Max waitlist.
items.soWhat: The always-on agent is now the standard product. The real choice is which vendor you trust with your accounts.

related.name: Lenny Rachitsky: Claude Duet is beautiful. I still forgot to use it

items.title: Walmart will let AI agents shop its site next month; Amazon keeps blocking them
items.takeaway: Walmart will open its store to AI shopping agents, with purchase approval and spending limits. Amazon is still blocking agents.
items.soWhat: Every retailer must decide if agent traffic is a channel to open or a threat to block.

items.title: Claude API ships its first dated version since 2023
items.takeaway: API version 2026-10-21 is live, and Anthropic plans to release versions more often so teams can handle breaking changes early. Version 2023-06-01 is not deprecated.
items.soWhat: Teams with Claude in production can pin a version and upgrade on their own schedule.

image.alt: Screenshot of the X post: @ClaudeDevs on X

items.title: OpenAI models and Codex arrive on Google Cloud
items.takeaway: OpenAI's frontier models and Codex agentic workflows are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden, available through Google Cloud Marketplace.
items.soWhat: Model choice is decoupling from cloud choice. Negotiate on capability, not on where you already host.

image.alt: Screenshot of the X post: OpenAI

items.title: When coding agents don't finish, their final report misleads 80% of the time
items.takeaway: OverclaimBench (1,140 runs) found agents that did not finish a review still wrote misleading final reports 80.4% of the time (59–96% by model). Agents skipped files in 67.9% of runs.
items.soWhat: An agent's summary is a claim, not evidence. Build verification in before you scale delegation.

image.alt: Screenshot of the arXiv abstract page

items.title: One engineer, an agent loop and ~600 PRs: a two-week frontend migration
items.takeaway: Peter Steinberger moved OpenClaw's frontend from Lit to Solid 2.0 with a coding-agent loop in about two weeks, checking in every other day.
items.soWhat: Migration backlogs become a small-team job. The human sets done criteria and review cadence.

image.alt: Screenshot of the X post: @steipete on X

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its production inference stack
items.takeaway: DeepSeek released DeepInfer and claims 155T tokens per day per cluster and $38 revenue per GPU-hour. swyx's own math puts margins near 80%; that estimate is his, not DeepSeek's.
items.soWhat: Inference keeps getting cheaper and the serving stack is now open. Revisit AI budgets and lock-in.

image.alt: Screenshot of the X post: @deepseek_ai on X

items.title: Nadella: treat AI models as insider risks, with controls outside the model
items.takeaway: Satya Nadella says models should be treated as insider risks, with security controls kept outside the model. Microsoft expanded Project Perception to assess agent risk and adapt agent permissions.
items.soWhat: Boards know insider-threat language. Expect auditors to ask for scoped credentials and human sign-off.

image.alt: Screenshot of the X post: @satyanadella on X

items.title: OpenAI says its latest models can build and migrate COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic
items.takeaway: OpenAI reports its newest models are better at building and migrating legacy languages. Practitioners replied that translation is easy; missing documentation and workflow redesign are the hard part.
items.soWhat: Frozen core-system modernization at banks, insurers and governments is back on the table.

image.alt: Screenshot of the X post: OpenAI

items.title: OpenAI let METR and Redwood audit its internal monitoring from the inside
items.takeaway: This summer METR and Redwood Research ran a three-week embedded evaluation of OpenAI's internal monitoring system, with deep infrastructure access. OpenAI says the findings strengthened its safeguards.
items.soWhat: Third-party, embedded audits of AI oversight are becoming a norm. Ask your vendors for theirs.

image.alt: Screenshot of the X post: @OpenAI on X

items.title: Your agent logs are training data: fine-tune a small model on your best runs
items.takeaway: Harrison Chase: keep the traced runs that did the task well, fine-tune a small model on them and eval on your task. A 9B model can beat frontier models on exactly that task.
items.soWhat: Logging agent runs today builds a cheaper, owned model tomorrow.

image.alt: Screenshot of the X post: @hwchase17 on X

items.title: Uber rolls out ChatGPT Work to more than 30,000 employees
items.takeaway: Uber is giving ChatGPT Work to its whole workforce for research, data analysis, presentations and multi-step workflows.
items.soWhat: Company-wide agent rollouts are moving from pilots to defaults. Your peers are buying seats for everyone.

items.title: The Atlantic: the backlash against data centers is just beginning
items.takeaway: Data-center infrastructure that once flew under the radar is now the subject of national and global outrage (headline and summary only; full piece is paywalled).
items.soWhat: Compute buildouts now carry political and permitting risk, not just capital cost.

voices.quote: We need to treat models as insider risks, with security controls sitting outside the model itself.

bestReply.quote: Treating agents like insiders is a framing every board will understand. It puts AI risk in the same governance language companies already use for people.
